statement: For an ideal \(J\subset A\), \(M/JM\cong M\otimes_A A/J\) is an \(A/J\)-module. It is a vector space when \(J\) is maximal. The geometric fibre at a prime \(\mathfrak p\) is \(M\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)\), not in general \(M/\mathfrak p M\). For \(A=\mathbb Z[t_1,t_2,\ldots]\) and integers \(a_i\), the displayed evaluation ideal has quotient \(\mathbb Z\), so it is prime but not maximal; a residue characteristic must also be imposed to obtain the corresponding finite-characteristic point.
reconstruction: The correction already begun in the notebook is completed. Points lie in \(\operatorname{Spec}A\), not in the module \(M\); an ideal is a subset of \(A\), not a subset of the scheme \(\mathbb A\).
fate: This is the ordinary affine-scheme meaning of fibre. The same coefficient-scheme viewpoint underlies \citet[Section 1.0]{morava1985noetherian}; that later account clarifies the geometry rather than introducing the elementary tensor-product identity.
present_status: As of November 2026, the construction is standard. Keeping the base ring prevents a false vector-space assertion and clarifies the varying coefficient fields of the height strata.

title: Full and strict formal coordinate changes
notes: The group consists of \(g(x)=a_1x+a_2x^2+\cdots\). Both \(a_1=1\) and the condition that \(a_1\) be a unit occur. Laws are equivalent under \(F_1=\varphi^{-1}F_2(\varphi(x),\varphi(y))\).
statement: For any commutative ring \(R\), series \(g\in xR[[x]]\) with invertible linear coefficient form a group under substitution. The inverse is found recursively. The subgroup with \(g'(0)=1\) consists of strict coordinate changes; over \(\mathbb Z\), the full group permits \(g'(0)=\pm1\). Isomorphism of one-dimensional formal group laws means an invertible series intertwining the laws, equivalently the displayed conjugation formula.
reconstruction: The two linear-coefficient conditions specify different groups, not interchangeable conventions. The ambiguous margin phrase translated as ``same-form groups'' means isomorphic formal groups in the displayed formula.
fate: Formal changes of coordinate are part of Lazard's pre-seminar theory \citep{lazard1955formal}. Their full/strict distinction and grading are explicit in \citet[Sections 1.0.2--1.0.4]{morava1985noetherian}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the construction is established over arbitrary commutative rings, with invertibility required only for the linear coefficient.

title: Formal vector fields and the ambiguous dual of differentials
notes: The margin names \(W_1\), the algebra of formal vector fields, and \(W'_1\), a ``dual algebra of differentials'', without specifying the duality or its operations.
statement: Over a characteristic-zero field \(k\), the formal vector fields are \(W_1=k[[x]]\partial_x\), with \([f\partial_x,g\partial_x]=(fg'-gf')\partial_x\). The module of formal differentials \(k[[x]]\,dx\) is dual to this rank-one module over \(k[[x]]\). This module dual is distinct from the continuous \(k\)-linear dual of the infinite-dimensional Lie algebra. The Lie algebra of origin-fixing formal substitutions is the subalgebra \(xk[[x]]\partial_x\).
reconstruction: These are precise nearby constructions, not an identification of the unexplained prime on \(W'_1\). No Lie bracket on the differential module, topology for a continuous dual, or claim about a coadjoint representation is supplied by the notes.
fate: The distinctions are explicit in the modern formal-geometry treatment \citet[Section 2.1 and Corollary 2.5.18]{gorbounov2020chiral}. Searches for formal vector fields, dual differentials and Gelfand--Fuks terminology recover that framework, but no exact additional theorem can be assigned to this isolated line.
present_status: As of November 2026, the elementary objects are standard, but the intended meaning of ``dual algebra'' remains unidentified in this occurrence. This is a limitation of the record, not evidence of an undeveloped mathematical idea.

title: Associativity and the characteristic-zero commutativity theorem
notes: A law \(F=x+y+\alpha xy+\beta x^2y+\delta xy^2+\cdots\) is said to have associativity as its sole requirement. On the next page, over a field of characteristic zero, it is declared isomorphic to addition and hence commutative.
statement: Let \(R\) be a \(\mathbb Q\)-algebra and let \(F\in R[[x,y]]\) satisfy \(F(x,0)=x\), \(F(0,y)=y\) and associativity. Writing \(f(x)=\partial_2F(x,0)\), define \(\ell(x)=\int_0^x dt/f(t)\). Then \(\ell(F(x,y))=\ell(x)+\ell(y)\); thus \(F\) is isomorphic to the additive law and is commutative. Over arbitrary rings, associativity and the displayed identity terms define a possibly noncommutative one-dimensional law; commutativity cannot be silently added.
reconstruction: \ours{} Differentiating associativity in its third variable at zero gives \(f(F(x,y))=\partial_2F(x,y)f(y)\). Consequently the derivative in \(y\) of \(\ell(F(x,y))\) is \(\ell'(y)\); the value at \(y=0\) gives the stated identity. This checks the notebook's logarithm argument without assuming commutativity first. The integral uses division by all positive integers.
fate: Characteristic-zero logarithms are classical formal-group theory \citep{lazard1955formal}; the normalized logarithm and rational coefficient requirement are explicit in \citet[Section 1]{quillen1969formal}. The derivation above is our check of the slightly stronger associative formulation used by the notes.
present_status: As of November 2026, the characteristic-zero field assertion is established. Its unrestricted-ring extrapolation is invalid; integral and positive-characteristic formal groups require separate hypotheses.

title: Invariant differentials, pullback and the obstruction to integration
notes: The invariant differential is \(a(x)dx=dx/f(x)\); its integral gives the inverse coordinate. The substitution rule is \(a(x)\mapsto a(\varphi(x))\varphi'(x)\). The text says any series \(a(x)=1+a_1x+\cdots\) determines a formal group, and notes that \(\int x^{p-1}dx\) does not exist in characteristic \(p\).
statement: Over a \(\mathbb Q\)-algebra, every \(a(x)\in1+xR[[x]]\) has the unique normalized primitive \(\ell(x)=x+\sum_{n\geq1}a_nx^{n+1}/(n+1)\). The law \(\ell^{-1}(\ell(x)+\ell(y))\) has normalized invariant differential \(a(x)dx\). For a strict change \(\varphi'(0)=1\), pullback sends its coefficient to \(a(\varphi(x))\varphi'(x)\). For a full coordinate change, the normalized differential acquires the additional factor \(1/\varphi'(0)\). In characteristic \(p\), the derivative of every power series has zero coefficient at \(x^{p-1}\), so that monomial has no primitive.
reconstruction: The scope remains the characteristic-zero field in the preceding theorem, or more generally a \(\mathbb Q\)-algebra. Arbitrary pullback one-forms need not remain normalized. The isolated dot above the second inverse-coordinate symbol is not interpreted as an extra derivative; that reading would contradict the displayed integral.
fate: The invariant differential and logarithm formulas are in \citet[Section 1, equations (1)--(2)]{quillen1969formal}, before the seminar. The substitution factor follows from the usual pullback of one-forms and the choice of normalization.
present_status: As of November 2026, the rational correspondence is established. The universal Lazard ring does not remove the positive-characteristic integration obstruction or make every normalized differential over an arbitrary ring arise by this logarithm formula.

title: Mishchenko’s projective-space coefficients
notes: Morava identifies the coefficients of \(a(x)\) with \([\mathbb {CP}^1],[\mathbb {CP}^2],\ldots\), citing Mishchenko; the page also records a suggestion by Kirillov.
statement: For the formal group law of the canonical complex orientation of \(MU\), its normalized invariant differential and rational logarithm are \[\omega_F(x)=\left(\sum_{n\geq0}[\mathbb {CP}^{n}]x^n\right)dx,\qquad \log_F(x)=\sum_{n\geq0}\frac{[\mathbb {CP}^{n}]}{n+1}x^{n+1},\] with \([\mathbb {CP}^{0}]=1\). The differential has integral bordism coefficients; the logarithm is taken in \(MU_*\otimes\mathbb Q\), with grading interpreted in the usual complex-oriented convention.
reconstruction: The denominator belongs in the logarithm, not in the differential. A complex orientation and its coordinate are fixed; arbitrary polynomial generators of \(MU_*\) are not being equated with every projective-space class.
fate: \citet[Corollary to Theorem 1]{quillen1969formal} explicitly credits Mishchenko and gives the logarithm formula. Its differential is exactly the coefficient assertion recorded here, already published in 1969.
present_status: As of November 2026, the formula is established. It connects geometric projective-space classes with the formal-group logarithm and supplies a precise bridge between the two parts of the lecture.

title: When a transitive group-scheme action is a homogeneous quotient
notes: The final theorem assumes a smooth \(G\)-scheme \(X\) over \(\mathbb Z\), a flat group scheme \(G\), noetherian hypotheses, and transitivity of \(G(K)\) on \(X(K)\) for an algebraically closed field. The continuation asserts \(X\cong G/S\), with \(S\) a stabilizer.
statement: A precise field version is the following. Let \(k\) be algebraically closed, \(G\) a smooth affine algebraic group over \(k\), and \(X\) a nonempty separated reduced finite-type \(k\)-scheme on which \(G(k)\) acts transitively. For \(x\in X(k)\), the scheme-theoretic stabilizer \(S=G_x\) is closed and the orbit map identifies \(X\) with the faithfully flat quotient \(G/S\). The stabilizer need not be reduced. Over a base such as \(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z\), a corresponding quotient description needs a global section and a faithfully flat orbit map. Geometric-point transitivity alone does not supply those data.
reconstruction: The verified statement is explicitly restricted to a field. The manuscript's quantifier before \(K\) is crossed out, and geometric-fibre transitivity does not itself provide a chosen global section or a globally defined stabilizer over \(\mathbb Z\). Nor do finite-type noetherian hypotheses automatically apply to the infinite-dimensional formal-coordinate group used earlier.
fate: The orbit and quotient theorem is established algebraic-group theory; see \citet[Propositions 7.11--7.17, especially Remark 7.16(c)]{milne2017groups}. This gives a verified precise core, not verification of the stronger relative formulation exactly as abbreviated in the notebook.
present_status: As of November 2026, the field theorem and the faithfully flat orbit criterion are established. The intended full relative theorem remains underdetermined by the cancelled quantifier and missing section data.

title: Gelfand’s programme of quantizing existing equations
notes: Gelfand's first task is \ru{проквантовать существующ. ур-я}: quantize the existing equations.
statement: No specific classical equation, phase space, quantization rule, dimension or required quantum theory is supplied. The line therefore states a research programme; it cannot be converted into a definite existence or uniqueness question without adding its mathematical object and success criterion.
reconstruction: The neighbouring Nelson discussion suggests constructive quantum field theory as context, but does not determine whether Gelfand intended a particular polynomial interaction or a canonical quantization prescription.
fate: Contemporary context is supplied by \citet[Introduction and Section 1]{cartier1974quantum}, whose November 1972 lecture discusses explicit scalar-field equations and the gap between formal equations and construction. That is thematic evidence, not an exact match for the unspecified equation in this occurrence.
present_status: As of November 2026, the problem cannot be identified at the level required for an open-problem entry. No claim about its solution, insolubility or lack of later work follows from this shorthand.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Gelfand’s programme of finding physically adequate equations
notes: The second task is to write equations that really correspond to physics; no model or observable is named.
statement: This is a request to choose a physically adequate dynamical model. The notes contain no mathematical class of equations, data to be reproduced, accuracy criterion, or existence assertion. A precise modern formulation cannot be supplied from this record alone.
reconstruction: The distinction from the first task is preserved: constructing a quantum theory for a specified classical model and selecting that model are different questions. Neither is identified with a later named conjecture.
fate: The model-construction discussion in \citet[Section 1.5]{cartier1974quantum} provides contemporary background. Searches centered on Dobrushin, Nelson and the listed date did not identify a particular equation or claim corresponding to Gelfand's second programme.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Euclidean-invariant random fields and the spatial Markov property
notes: Dobrushin writes random quantities \(\xi_t\), indexed by \(t\in\mathbb R^{\nu+1}\), satisfying Euclidean invariance and the Markov property.
statement: A random generalized scalar field is a continuous linear map \(T:\mathcal S(\mathbb R^d)\to L^0(\Omega,\mathbb P)\), where \(L^0\) carries convergence in probability. Euclidean invariance means equality of joint laws after every Euclidean isometry. Let \(\mathcal F(U)\) be generated by field tests supported in an open region \(U\), and choose a specified boundary sigma-field \(\mathcal F(\partial U)\). The spatial Markov property says that, for integrable \(\mathcal F(U)\)-measurable \(Z\), \(\mathbb E[Z\mid\mathcal F(U^c)]=\mathbb E[Z\mid\mathcal F(\partial U)]\). This concerns conditional independence of spatial regions, not merely a one-parameter Markov process.
reconstruction: Generalized fields replace pointwise random variables because the latter need not exist. The boundary sigma-field is part of the definition: in the Sobolev formulation below it is generated by the extended field evaluated on supported \(H^{-1}\) distributions. It must not automatically be replaced by an intersection of neighbourhood sigma-fields.
fate: This is Nelson's framework, already described in \citet[Section 3.1 and note (3), p. 27]{cartier1974quantum}, a November 1972 lecture published in 1974. Nelson's own bibliography dates the initial Berkeley exposition to August 1971, with proceedings publication in 1973 \citep{nelson1973quantum}.
present_status: As of November 2026, the framework is established. The notebook's two labels identify the method but do not specify the analytic regularity needed for a reconstruction theorem.

title: Nelson reconstruction with explicit analytic assumptions
notes: The main author of a probabilistic method for constructing objects satisfying the Wightman axioms is identified as Nelson. Only Euclidean invariance and a Markov property are written.
statement: One precise version, in four Euclidean dimensions, starts with a real random tempered distribution \(T\) whose law is invariant under all Euclidean isometries, including reflection. Assume that \(T\) extends continuously to \(H^{-1}(\mathbb R^4)\). For closed \(F\), let \(\mathcal F(F)\) be generated by \(T(u)\) with \(u\in H^{-1}\) supported in \(F\), and impose the spatial Markov property with these sigma-fields. Conditional expectation and time translation then give a strongly continuous self-adjoint contraction semigroup \(e^{-tH}\), \(H\geq0\), on \(L^2(\Omega,\mathcal F(\{t=0\}),\mathbb P)\). Put \(\phi_0(u)=T(u\otimes\delta_0)\). Assume in addition that some integer \(m\geq0\) satisfies \[\int |\phi_0(u)|\,|\Phi|^2\,d\mathbb P<\infty\quad\text{for all }u\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3),\ \Phi\in D(H^m).\] Nelson's construction then yields smeared fields on the smooth domain of \(H\); restricting to the cyclic vacuum subspace gives temperedness, Poincar\'e covariance, the spectrum condition and local commutativity. Uniqueness of the invariant vacuum is not asserted without an additional ergodicity or clustering hypothesis.
